1. Overview & Motivation

In high-fidelity cinematic and mathematical visualizations, visual narratives rarely consist of isolated, independent movements. Instead, complex choreographies require **multi-stage temporal progression**:

items: **Staged Introductions**: Outlining a geometric boundary $\rightarrow$ Pausing $\rightarrow$ Fading in interior fill $\rightarrow$ Displaying mathematical annotations.
**State Anticipation & Settle**: Rapid expansion beyond equilibrium (anticipation/pop) $\rightarrow$ Elastic harmonic settling back to standard scale.
**Compound Storytelling**: Revealing an initial equation $\rightarrow$ Highlighting a specific variable $\rightarrow$ Morphing to a simplified term.

blocks.text: Retiam provides two complementary, first-class composite [`Animation`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/animation/Animation.ts) primitives based on the **Composite Pattern**:

items: [`Sequential`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/animation/Sequential.ts): Orchestrates an ordered list of animations **strictly in series** (one after another).

[`Concurrent`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/animation/Concurrent.ts): Orchestrates an ordered list of animations **simultaneously in parallel**, with optional start staggering via `lagRatio`.

blocks.text: Because both `Sequential` and `Concurrent` extend `Animation`, they can be passed directly to `scene.play()`, nested within each other to form arbitrary animation trees, or subclassed to create reusable, parameterizable visual effects.
2. Core Architectural Principles

children: `Concurrent` handles **temporal concurrence & parallel waves** ($A \parallel B \parallel C$).

items: **Composable Tree Hierarchy (Composite Pattern)**: A `Sequential` can contain atomic animations (`FadeIn`, `StateAnimation`, `Create`), parallel clusters (`Concurrent`), or nested sub-sequences.

children: In `Sequential`: Total duration is automatically computed as the sum of its constituent animations' durations ($\sum D_i$).
In `Concurrent`: Animations run simultaneously within the allotted `this.duration`, mathematically distributed according to `lagRatio`.

items: **Proportional Time Scaling**: Modifying the composite duration (via `scene.play(anim, { duration: T })` or `applyOptions`) scales each child's duration and delay proportionally, preserving the relative rhythm and choreography.

**Completion-Boundary Scheduling**: The scheduler divides a frame at real animation boundaries. Completion promises may queue the next work, which is advanced through the same frame's remaining time without exposing a timing remainder.
**Recursive State Preparation**: Calling `.prepare()` traverses the animation hierarchy, allowing all child animations to freeze their initial transforms and pre-bake paths before playback commences.

blocks.content: Passing `duration: scaledDuration, delay: scaledDelay` into `anim.applyOptions` ensures that if any child animation is a composite animation (such as `Concurrent`, `Create`, or a nested `Sequential`), the duration scales recursively down the entire animation hierarchy. Furthermore, `new Sequential(anims, { duration: T })` respects `options.duration` on initialization, proportionally scaling its children to fit $T$ rather than discarding the caller's target duration.

blocks.text: 4.2 Completion-Boundary Handoffs

Frames are scheduled around boundaries, not around a numeric timing value returned by an animation. If animation $A$ has 10 ms remaining in a 16.67 ms frame, the scheduler advances to that boundary, completes $A$, then resumes its play continuation.
The continuation can queue $B$ before the scheduler consumes the remaining 6.67 ms. $B$ therefore begins in the same rendered frame, without a one-frame gap or a user-visible balance-time value.
The same shared scheduler serves scene, composer, and nested scene queues; Sequential follows the same boundary contract for its children:

4.3 Concurrent: Stagger Distribution & Arc-Length Scheduling
Located at [`src/engine/animation/Concurrent.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/animation/Concurrent.ts):
`Concurrent` orchestrates child animations running simultaneously or in staggered sequences. It supports three staggering modes via `stagger` / `lagRatio`:

items: `stagger: 'simultaneous'` (`lagRatio = 0.0`): All child animations start at $t = 0$ with duration equal to `this.duration`.
`stagger: 'sequential'` (`lagRatio = 1.0`): Child animations execute strictly one after another in series.
`stagger: number` ($0 < \text{lagRatio} < 1.0$, e.g. `0.08`): Overlapping cascade wave where each subsequent child begins after fraction `lagRatio` of the previous child's duration.

blocks.text: Duration Distribution Strategies (distribution)

When animating composite vector entities comprising multiple paths (such as SVGs, Excalidraw sketches, and VGroups), dividing total time equally among all paths can cause tiny dots or accents to freeze on screen for hundreds of milliseconds while long outlines rush by.

Sub-linear power-law curve. Keeps micro-paths and dots snappy ($\approx 16\text{--}40\text{ms}$) while giving large outlines and hatches ample time.

Hierarchical Duration Propagation

In `Concurrent.applyOptions`, `duration: durations[index]` and `delay: delays[index]` are passed directly into each child's `anim.applyOptions(...)`. This enables nested composite structures (such as `Excalidraw.createAnim`, which groups `Create` and `BoilAnimation` in parallel) to propagate scaled durations down to all leaf paths.

7. Best Practices & Invariants

When passed to `new Sequential(anims)`, the sequence caches the sum of their initial durations. Do not manually mutate `anim.duration` directly on child objects after passing them into the sequence; use `seq.applyOptions({ duration: ... })` instead to trigger proportional recalculation.

`Sequential.prepare()` iterates over every child animation in forward order. If child animations depend on entity state transformations pre-calculated by earlier children, ensure states are cleanly copied (via `ent.state.copy()`) rather than mutated in place during initialization.

Use `Concurrent` to express *spatial concurrence* (what moves together) and `Sequential` to express *temporal progression* (what moves when). Combining both produces clean, tree-structured motion choreography with mathematical determinism.
